title: Freddie Keppard compared with Joe Oliver
summary: Shoffner says Keppard was a faster reader than Oliver, rougher and stronger with a different style, and used an open horn where Oliver used mutes.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Was Keppert much of a reader, do you remember? Yeah. He could read all right then. He could read all right. We never did know for sure.
He could read all right. He was a, well, he was a much, I would say a much faster reader than Joe Oliver.
Yeah, he was a much faster reader than Joe Oliver, you see. But he had a different style altogether. His style was, well, you couldn't compare the two, because he had a different style.
I've heard him on record, but I never heard either one of them in person.

No, he was just a strong, strong trumpet player. Was he rougher than Oliver? Oh yeah. Yeah, he's way rougher. Rougher. That's right. I thought that from the record. I mean, the record taker, at that time, I mean, like a 10 piece or 12 piece band, now you didn't need anybody to ever play together. Yeah. And he played all night. He just had an awful strong, strong lip. He would just play like that.
Did he ever use the muter hand much like Oliver used? Well, he used an open hand. No, that's right. Open, open hand. Open.
